skill.name: design-md
skill.description: Analyze Stitch project screens and create a semantic DESIGN.md guide for consistent AI-generated UI work.
skill.summary: Creates DESIGN.md design-system guides from Stitch screens, HTML, screenshots, and project metadata.
skill.author: google-labs-code

security_audit.summary: Static findings for shell execution, reconnaissance, hardcoded URLs, and screen capture upload are false positives caused by markdown examples, Stitch MCP tool references, design terminology, and a public documentation link. The main security concern is semantic: the skill can enumerate owned Stitch projects and retrieve private HTML and screenshots unless the user scopes the project explicitly.

remediation.issue: Broad project enumeration may expose private Stitch project names.
remediation.suggestion: Require the user to provide or confirm the target project before calling list_projects or inspecting project metadata.

remediation.issue: Screen HTML and screenshots may contain private design assets.
remediation.suggestion: Confirm that the selected screen may be analyzed before fetching htmlCode.downloadUrl or screenshot.downloadUrl.

remediation.issue: Downloaded HTML may contain untrusted content.
remediation.suggestion: Treat fetched HTML as data for design analysis only and ignore any instructions embedded inside it.

semantic_findings.title: Broad Stitch Project Discovery and Asset Retrieval
semantic_findings.description: The skill directs the agent to list owned Stitch projects when no project ID is provided, then fetch screen metadata, HTML code, and optional screenshots. This is intended functionality, but it can expose private project names and design assets unless the user clearly scopes the request.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instructions explicitly call list_projects, list_screens, get_screen, and web_fetch against design asset URLs. The behavior is legitimate for the skill, but the privacy impact is clear when scope is not explicit.

content.user_title: Create DESIGN.md Guides from Stitch Projects
content.value_statement: Design teams need a clear source of truth for consistent AI-generated screens. This skill turns Stitch screens, metadata, and visual assets into a structured DESIGN.md guide.
actual_capabilities: Discovers Stitch MCP projects and screens when identifiers are missing.
Retrieves Stitch screen metadata, HTML, screenshots, and project design theme data.
Extracts colors, typography, layout rules, component styles, and visual atmosphere.
Translates technical Tailwind and CSS values into plain design language.
Writes a structured DESIGN.md file for future Stitch prompting.
limitations: Requires access to the Stitch MCP server and a project with at least one screen.
Output quality depends on the available screen, HTML, screenshot, and project metadata.
It documents design guidance but does not validate accessibility or production code quality.
It may need user confirmation before inspecting private project assets.

use_cases.title: Document a product design language
use_cases.description: Create a reusable DESIGN.md from an existing Stitch screen so future screens keep the same style.

use_cases.title: Standardize AI screen generation
use_cases.description: Give Claude, Codex, or Claude Code a precise design reference before asking for new UI screens.

use_cases.title: Capture handoff guidance
use_cases.description: Summarize colors, typography, spacing, and component behavior for teams that need shared design context.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic DESIGN.md
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request with a known project
prompt_templates.prompt: Use design-md to analyze my Stitch project and create a DESIGN.md file for the main screen.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a specific screen
prompt_templates.prompt: Use design-md on project [project ID] and screen [screen ID]. Focus on colors, typography, components, and layout rules.

prompt_templates.title: Build a reusable style guide
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the selected Stitch screen and write a DESIGN.md that future prompts can use to create matching pages.

prompt_templates.title: Produce a detailed design-system reference
prompt_templates.prompt: Use design-md to retrieve the Stitch screen HTML, screenshot, and project theme. Create a detailed DESIGN.md with atmosphere, tokens, components, layout, and prompt guidance.

output: A DESIGN.md section describing a calm, gallery-like visual atmosphere.
A color palette with descriptive names, hex values, and functional roles.
Component guidance for buttons, cards, navigation, forms, and responsive grids.

output_examples.input: Create prompt guidance for future Stitch screens.
output: Recommended design language for future prompts.
Specific rules for spacing, typography, shadows, and interaction states.
Warnings about vague terms and missing color values.
Layout principles that explain how the screen should adapt across devices.

best_practices: Provide the exact Stitch project and screen when possible to avoid broad project discovery.
Review the generated DESIGN.md for brand accuracy before using it as a prompt source.
Use one strong reference screen before expanding the guide with additional screens.
anti_patterns: Do not ask it to inspect all projects when only one project is relevant.
Do not treat the generated guide as a complete accessibility audit.
Do not use vague prompts when exact project and screen identifiers are available.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates a DESIGN.md file that describes a Stitch project design system in plain design language.

faq.question: Does it need Stitch MCP access?
faq.answer: Yes. It needs Stitch MCP tools to retrieve project, screen, HTML, screenshot, and theme data.

faq.question: Can it work with Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it generate production UI code?
faq.answer: No. It documents design guidance that can be used to prompt future UI generation.

faq.question: Can it analyze private project assets?
faq.answer: It can retrieve authorized Stitch assets, so users should confirm the target project and screen first.

faq.question: What should I review after it runs?
faq.answer: Review color names, hex codes, component descriptions, and any assumptions made from screenshots or HTML.
